_doc: Radio stations. The boat radio scans stations with R. A station broadcasts its lines in order on a loop; gap = seconds between lines. 'night' stations only come in after dark. Lines can set a story flag the first time they are heard.

stations.name: 88.1 — Highmark Supply Authority
lines: This is the Highmark Supply Authority. The time is now. The tide is steady.
Ration collection for the Orrin Bay districts will take place on the third day. Please have your tally ready.
Citizens are reminded that work permits are available to those who demonstrate reliable labour.
Tide Warden vessels operate for your protection. Please comply with all instructions.
There is no evidence of renewed illness. Keep two arms apart as a courtesy.
Reports of sounds or lights in the deep water are the result of settling structures. There is no cause for concern.
Order and supply. Supply and order. Highmark is with you.
[a soft chime] This has been the Highmark Supply Authority.

stations.name: 3.3 — (unregistered)
lines: [static] ...the Unmoored. If you can hear this, you are not alone on the water.
Nine six. One two eight. Minus. Nine six. One two eight. Minus.
The place where the plaza fell. Lower the ear at night. Listen to what Highmark listens to.
Nine six. One two eight. Minus. [static] ...counting down. It is counting down.
Do not trust the Wardens. Do not trust the seal. Trust the water. It does not lie about how deep it is.
